model.notes: Read from the file's flatbuffer on 2026-11-18: one signature 'serving_default', 1,408 operators of 32 built-in kinds, no custom ops, two IF branches inside the model's own preprocessing.

parts.name: face
parts.source: Face Landmarker points 0-467 (the 468-point mesh; the 10 iris points 468-477 are dropped)

parts.name: left_hand
parts.source: the signer's left hand, as assigned by features_v2.canonicalize_frame

parts.name: right_hand
parts.source: the signer's right hand, as assigned by features_v2.canonicalize_frame

layout.notes: The Google Isolated Sign Language Recognition data layout: per frame the parquet rows are face, left_hand, pose, right_hand.

conventions.coordinates: x and y are normalised coordinates of the upright, unmirrored camera frame; z is MediaPipe's own relative depth for that part
conventions.hand_slots_status: assumed; notebooks/asl_mode_eval.ipynb measures it on the rerun set (hand wrists against pose wrists, and which slot holds the dominant hand)
conventions.mirrored_input: refused: the 468-point face mesh has no mirror map here, so callers pass unmirrored frames and mirror only what they display

segmentation.rule: A sign starts on the first frame with a hand and ends after end_after_missing_frames frames without hands. It keeps margin_frames frames before and after. Signs with fewer than min_hand_frames frames that show a hand are dropped; a sign is cut at max_frames.

fixed_length.rule: nearest-frame resampling: for T > 1, output frame i is input frame floor((2*i*(L-1) + (T-1)) / (2*(T-1))); for T = 1 it is frame 0
fixed_length.used_by: the browser runtime only: LiteRT.js cannot take a variable number of frames, so the model's input is rewritten to frames x 543 x 3 before it is compiled
fixed_length.status: 32 is a starting value; notebooks/asl_mode_eval.ipynb compares 16, 24, 32, 48 and 64 frames with the native variable length

words.unsure: Not sure. Is it one of these?
words.none: I'm not sure. Try once more.

confidence.status: sure/unsure: starting values (kept: they define the frozen baseline's words). speak_at 0.70 measured on 2026-11-20 (GISLR rerun set, 39,443 signs, reports/asl_eval_results_2026-11-20.json): at >= 0.60, 97.2 % of answers were right (2.8 % wrong); at >= 0.70, 98.3 % (1.7 % wrong), meeting master-v3's limit of 2 % wrong words spoken aloud.
